observations.says: at four o'clock on Saturday, somebody handed in the telegram at the post office at Leeds
from three o'clock on Saturday until five o'clock on Saturday, Mary Holt was at the church fête
at two o'clock on Saturday, Mr. Martin Grove took the train to Leeds
at eleven o'clock on Saturday night, the telegram was written out in the post office clerk's hand, not the sender's
taking it that Mr. Martin Grove handed in the telegram at the post office at Leeds: at eleven o'clock on Saturday night, the telegram said: "Come to the mill at ten. M."
taking it that Mary Holt handed in the telegram at the post office at Leeds: at eleven o'clock on Saturday night, the telegram said: "Come to the mill at ten. M."

at half past nine on Saturday night, Mr. Martin Grove drew the key of Dyer's Mill; from half past nine on Saturday night until ten o'clock on Saturday night, nobody but Mr. Martin Grove had a key of Dyer's Mill
